headline: Agreed to send a councilor code of conduct, a staff interactions policy, and ethics ordinance changes to City Council
summary: Four items, including respect for staff, will move into a section councilors must follow. A separate policy on interactions with staff and commissions can be enforced by the Council itself, without a Board of Ethics process. The ethics ordinance will let the Board of Ethics review complaints in non-public meetings under RSA 91-A:3, II, and goes to a December public hearing.
decisions: Approved the September 28, 2026 meeting minutes with no dissenting votes.
Agreed to have the Legal Department make requested edits to the code of conduct and send it to City Council in November.
Agreed to advance the policy on interactions with staff and commissions to City Council for its November meeting, with one edit.
Agreed to send the Board of Ethics ordinance, with the non-public meeting edit, to City Council for a December public hearing.

plain_text:
City Council Rules Committee  
Draft Meeting Minutes 
October 20, 2026   
City Council Chambers 
37 Green Street 
3:00 PM  
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Councilor Kretovic called the meeting to order at 3:03 PM. 
 
2. Roll Call 
 
Present: Chair Jennifer Kretovic, Councilor Jeff Foote, Councilor Judith Kurtz, Councilor 
Brent Todd 
 
Excused: Councilor Amanda Grady Sexton 
 
Also Present:  City Solicitor John Conforti, Jason Gerhart of Northfield, NH 
 
3. Approval of Meeting Minutes 
 
• September 28, 2026 Draft Meeting Minutes 
 
Councilor Todd moved approval of the September 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes.  The 
motion was duly seconded by Councilor Foote and passed with no dissenting votes. 
 
Councilor Kurtz arrived after this approval and was not present for the vote. 
 
4. Meeting overview  
 
Chair Kretovic reviewed the items for discussion. 
 
5. Items to be Considered Regarding the Amendment of Council Rules/Ethics 
Ordinance.
2 
• Code of Conduct. 
 
Councilor Kretovic summarized the prior discussions of the Committee on this topic and 
that the document that was reviewed in September has been separated into two 
documents for consideration. One document creates a clear code of conduct for City 
Councilors. Councilor Kretovic noted that the changes in the document being presented 
are in line with the edits requested at the September meeting.  
 
Councilor Foote noted that the code is reflective and may be duplicative of the Charter. 
Councilor Todd agreed with Councilor Foote but noted that it would be beneficial to have 
all of the information in one place, particularly for new Councilors.  
 
Councilor Todd noted that there were some items in the document that were worded as 
items that Councilors “should” do when in fact they were legal requirements. The 
Committee then discussed changing some items to a section that would require that 
Councilors “shall” comply with standard.  
 
Councilor Kurtz agreed and stated that the respect for the role of staff should go into the 
shall category.  
 
Councilor Kurtz asked about the items relating to conduct of the meetings and whether 
there are governing parliamentary procedures that should be included. Councilor 
Kretovic and Mr. Conforti discussed that the parliamentary procedures are laid out in the 
Council Rules. Councilor Todd noted that the language in the document was changed to 
presiding officer to ensure that it would apply if Mayor Pro-Tem or another Councilor 
was running the meeting. 
 
The Committee agreed to edit the draft document to move four items to a “shall” section. 
The four items were identified as: complying with the law, working for the common 
good, adhering to their oaths, and respecting the role of staff.  
 
Councilor Foote requested that the Committee consider revisions to the active listening 
portion of the document indicating that there are many ways to be an active listener and 
that the existing language is prescriptive. Councilor Todd, Councilor Kretovic and 
Councilor Kurtz all spoke in favor of that change. The Committee agreed to edit the 
document to simplify the section by stating that Councilors should remain focused on the 
speaker to the best of their ability.    
 
The Committee agreed to have the Legal Department complete the requested edits and 
submit the document for consideration to City Council in November.
3 
 
• Policy on Interactions With Staff and Commissions 
 
Councilor Kretovic reviewed the policy document that was previously taken out of the 
Code of Conduct and placed on its own because it has more concrete and enforceable 
provisions. Councilor Kretovic noted that the Council can enforce this themselves and do 
not need to go through a Board of Ethics process.  
 
Councilor Foote again noted that this is duplicative of existing legal requirements. Mr. 
Conforti agreed and noted that he views this like an administrative rule in that it provides 
further clarity and guidance on the existing Charter and Rule requirements. Councilor 
Todd noted the value of having a clear guideline of their legal obligations not just for 
Councilors but for the public. Councilor Kurtz agreed and noted that she liked the clarity 
of the document.  
 
Councilor Todd suggested one non-substantive edit to the document. 
 
The Committee agreed to advance this to City Council for consideration at the November 
meeting with the edit noted by Councilor Todd. 
 
• Board of Ethics Ordinance Change 
 
Councilor Kretovic noted that we have been discussing this matter for a significant 
amount of time and the primary question is whether complaints should be confidential 
before they go the Board for review. She noted that people are being named in complaints 
that are not the subject of the complaint and are not officers or officials of the City but 
nonetheless get the publicity of being named in the document. Councilor Kretovic noted 
that this would just control our process and that others may choose to post complaints on 
their own.  
 
Councilor Todd asked whether reputational damage was the only basis for a non-public 
meeting of the BOE. Mr. Conforti stated that this was the most likely reason why a 
meeting would be non-public, but that the Board operated under RSA 91-A and they 
would still have the right to go into non-public for other reasons so long as it met one of 
the statutory requirements.  
 
The Committee agreed to remove the specific provision related to reputational harm and 
instead have a provision that states that the BOE can review complaints in a non-public 
meeting in accordance with 91-A:3, II.
4 
Councilor Kurtz asked about the statute of limitations component of the ordinance and 
asked where a limitation is necessary. Councilor Kretovic discussed that there is currently 
no limitation and that creates challenged which is why statutes of limitations exist. Mr. 
Conforti noted that it can be difficult for all parties when a claim is old as documents, 
witnesses and memories can be less available. Mr. Conforti noted this could be difficult 
for the subject of the complaint to be able to respond to allegations that are from a decade 
ago. 
 
The Committee agreed to submit the ordinance, with the edit on non-public meetings, to 
the City Council for a December public hearing.  
 
6. Other Business 
 
7. Scheduling of Next Meeting 
 
The Committee noted that it does not need another meeting at this time and may 
reconvene in early 2027 depending on the outcome of Council action on these items.  
 
8. Adjournment 
 
At 4:07 PM, there being no additional business to discuss, Councilor Foote moved to 
adjourn.  The motion was duly seconded by Councilor Kurtz, and passed with no 
dissenting votes. 
 
A true copy; I attest: 
 
 
John Conforti 
City Solicitor 
 
This meeting is open to the public although there is no public input or testimony.
